currentContext.business: Following the acquisition of shares from the erstwhile promoters under a Share Purchase Agreement dated June 26, 2025 and completion of the mandatory Open Offer under the SEBI Takeover Regulations, control of the Company passed to a new promoter group and the Company diversified into the telecommunications sector. It commenced activities relating to telecom and allied services, including communication infrastructure, telecom solutions, network-related services, digital communication services and other ancillary activities. Its current operations are described in the MD&A as primarily fibre-leasing: creating, acquiring, leasing, operating and monetising optical fibre routes for telecom operators, internet service providers, enterprises, data centre operators and government agencies.

currentContext.expansion: The annual report contains no named capex project, no commissioning or ramp timeline and no rupee quantum. Expansion is described only as intent: following the change in management and control completed on January 5, 2026, the Company diversified into the telecommunications sector and commenced telecom and allied services (communication infrastructure, telecom solutions, network-related services and digital communication services), and the MD&A states its strategic focus is to create, acquire, lease, operate and monetise fibre infrastructure in a disciplined and scalable manner. Under 'Expansion of strategic fibre routes' the Company says it intends to strengthen its fibre network across commercially attractive routes - telecom-dense corridors, urban clusters, semi-urban growth centres, industrial areas, data centre locations and regions with rising broadband demand - with priority to routes with clear leasing potential and long-term monetisation visibility. Development is to be capital-efficient: prioritising high-demand routes, sharing infrastructure where feasible, using scalable network architecture and leveraging leasing opportunities instead of speculative build-outs, balancing growth against return on capital employed. The MD&A itself flags that the fibre leasing business is capital-intensive and requires substantial upfront investment in network development, permissions, execution, maintenance and monitoring, and that Right of Way and local permission delays may affect project timelines and cost efficiency. No route kilometres, no network footprint, no site or plant locations and no capex amount are disclosed anywhere in the routed text.

the Amended BharatNet Programme provides for optical fibre connectivity to 2.64 lakh Gram Panchayats, creating demand for fibre deployment, O&M, last-mile connectivity and leasing partnerships|Fibre-to-the-home and fixed broadband growth from OTT consumption, online education, gaming, work-from-home and smart home usage, increasing last-mile and middle-mile fibre demand|Infrastructure sharing and neutral-host models: operators focused on capital efficiency prefer leasing fibre to reduce upfront capex, accelerate rollouts and improve route diversity, supporting recurring revenue for owners of strategically located fibre assets|Policy tailwinds - National Broadband Mission 2.0, the Amended BharatNet Programme, the Gati Shakti Sanchar Portal, the Telecommunications Act, 2023 and the Telecommunications Right of Way Rules, 2024 effective January 1, 2025, which are expected to reduce delays and support faster execution of fibre projects|FY2025-26 performance driver stated by management: the improvement was driven primarily by the change in management and commencement/expansion of business operations under the new management, with the improved result attributable to commencement of business operations, increase in operational income and effective cost management|Offsetting pressures management names: competition from established telecom infrastructure companies and operators with captive fibre, pricing pressure, Right of Way and execution delays, customer concentration, fibre cuts and network downtime, and macro factors such as interest rates, input and labour cost inflation, funding constraints and delayed customer payments

risks.risk: Customer concentration - dependence on a limited number of large customers
risks.note: The MD&A states the Company may face dependence on a limited number of large customers, particularly telecom operators and infrastructure players, which can create customer concentration risk. With revenue from operations having started only in FY2025-26, the base is narrow and any single customer loss is disproportionately material.

risks.risk: Right of Way and permission delays
risks.note: Delays in obtaining Right of Way approvals, local permissions or utility clearances may affect project timelines and cost efficiency. Management also flags that changes in Right of Way charges or local-level execution challenges may adversely affect project economics, notwithstanding the Gati Shakti Sanchar Portal and the Telecommunications Right of Way Rules, 2024.

risks.risk: Capital intensity of the fibre leasing model
risks.note: The MD&A states the fibre leasing business is capital-intensive and requires substantial upfront investment in network development, permissions, execution, maintenance and monitoring - a heavy funding requirement for a company that has only just reported its first year of operating revenue and profitability.

risks.risk: Project execution risk - cost overruns, deployment delays, vendor dependency
risks.note: The Company says it is exposed to execution risks including cost overruns, delays in fibre deployment, vendor dependency, damage to underground infrastructure and disruption caused by civic works or third-party activity. The MD&A also notes returns depend on route selection, project execution capability and effective asset utilisation.

risks.risk: Network reliability - fibre cuts, downtime, theft and SLA failure
risks.note: Operational risks such as fibre cuts, network downtime, route disruptions, theft, damage and maintenance challenges may affect service quality and customer satisfaction; any prolonged downtime or failure to meet service-level commitments may impact customer relationships and revenue. In fibre leasing, reliability and maintenance are the stated differentiators.

risks.risk: Pricing pressure and competition from scaled and captive fibre owners
risks.note: Competition from established telecom infrastructure companies, telecom operators with captive fibre networks, internet service providers and regional fibre network owners may affect pricing, margins and customer acquisition - a structural disadvantage for a sub-scale new entrant.

The Company operates in a competitive and regulated industry; regulatory changes and delays in implementation of policy reforms may adversely affect project economics, and rapid technological developments may require continuous investment in network upgrades and operational capabilities.

risks.risk: Macro and working-capital exposure - interest rates, input cost inflation, funding constraints and delayed customer payments
risks.note: The MD&A names interest rate movements, inflation in materials and labour costs, funding constraints and delayed customer payments as factors that may affect profitability and cash flows, to be managed through prudent capital allocation, customer diversification, strong contracts and efficient operations.

risks.risk: Nascent scale - two employees, basic internal controls, and a business only months old
risks.note: The Company reports a permanent employee strength of 2 at March 31, 2026, describes its internal control systems as 'basic internal control systems commensurate with the current scale and nature of its operations', and says it is at a 'nascent stage of operations' still building its human resource base. Execution capacity, key-person dependence and control maturity are therefore genuine structural constraints on the stated growth plan.

risks.risk: Repeated changes of control and an unsettled ownership structure
risks.note: Control changed on January 5, 2026 via a Share Purchase Agreement with the erstwhile promoter and an Open Offer, with the entire Board reconstituted on that date; after year-end the Board's Report discloses that SAR Televenture Limited, as Acquirer, made a further Open Offer, with the Letter of Offer dispatched to shareholders on 2nd June, 2026. Strategy, management and the business model are therefore all newly installed and subject to further change.
